title: PDC Darts Player Career Earnings, Order of Merit Prize Money & Financial Analysis
source: PDC Official Order of Merit, Darts Database & Official Tournament Prize Fund Disclosures
financial_disclaimer: OFFICIAL PRIZE MONEY VS ESTIMATED NET WORTH: Figures cited in this directory represent official, audited prize money won in PDC-sanctioned ranking and invitational tournaments. Prize money does NOT equal net worth. Professional darts players operate as independent self-employed sports professionals subject to top-tier UK income taxes (up to 45%), manager/agent percentages (typically 10%–20%), European travel overheads, and coaching/physio costs. Commercial sponsorship deals (equipment manufacturers, betting partners, fashion) and exhibition appearance fees provide substantial additional revenue not captured in official Order of Merit statistics.

order_of_merit_structure.ranking_mechanism: Two-year rolling ranking based strictly on prize money won in PDC ranking events.
order_of_merit_structure.world_championship_weight: The World Championship is by far the most influential event on the calendar, offering a £500,000 winner's cheque that anchors a player's world ranking for 24 months.

Back-to-back World Championships (£250,000 in 2015, £300,000 in 2016) and 2018 World Matchplay (£115,000).

2023 World Championship title (£500,000), 2022 Grand Slam (£150,000), multi-year top-tier earner.
2021 World Championship (£500,000) and triple Grand Slam of Darts winner (£125,000–£150,000 each).
Rookie World Championship title in 2018 (£400,000) and 2019 World Matchplay (£150,000).
2023 World Matchplay Champion (£200,000) and 2019 UK Open (£100,000).
2024 World Championship (£500,000), 2024 World Matchplay (£200,000), 2023 Grand Slam (£150,000), 2023 World Grand Prix (£120,000).
2024 Masters Champion (£65,000) and consistent ProTour earnings.
